text:
Brandt Clarke is having the best five-on-five season of anyone on the Kings' blue line, and his point total barely shows it. Los Angeles takes 59.7% of the expected goals with him on the ice (expected goals measure chance quality), 14 points better than without him. That is not a sheltered number on a defenseman playing almost 20 minutes a night.

The scoreboard hasn't followed. The Kings have scored 8.2 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him out there, one of the biggest gaps in the league, and it has cost him assists. He still has 13 points in 18 games, six on the power play, but the team around him has lost seven of its last ten.

None of this is new information about his game. Evolving-Hockey had him 36th among defensemen last season, a play driver in the 91st percentile. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 99th percentile for primary shot assists among defensemen and stopping 16% of the entries aimed at him (typical is 11%). If the Kings' shooters start finishing what he sets up, his points will look like his play.
headline: Clarke is driving play and getting nothing for it
